records.name: Congregation Rodeph Shalom
records.summary: A Center City congregation on North Broad Street with Friday evening and Saturday morning services, Saturday Torah study, and a Wednesday morning food and supply distribution called Breaking Bread on Broad.
records.what_you_do: Come to Friday evening or Saturday morning services, or join Saturday Torah study. Newcomers can take one of two introductory courses on Judaism. Services are also livestreamed for people who would rather watch from home.

schedule.text: Friday pre-oneg at 5:30 pm, Friday Shabbat evening service at 6:00 pm, Saturday Torah study at 9:15 am, and Saturday morning service at 10:45 am. Breaking Bread on Broad distributes food and supplies on Wednesday mornings. Holiday services follow the full calendar.

cost.text: The Introduction to Judaism course is $250 per person or couple, and the three-session Taste of Judaism course is $36. Both are free for members. Membership dues and visitor fees for services are not stated on the site.

access.notes: The website has a toolbar for text size, contrast and underlined links. Wheelchair access, elevators and hearing help are not described on the site.

first_step.how: Come to the Friday 6 pm Shabbat evening service or the Saturday 10:45 am morning service at 615 N. Broad St., entering at 1339 Green St.
first_step.basis: The New to Judaism page lists two beginner courses and names a membership contact for newcomers, and the site invites everyone to Friday and Saturday services with no sign-up listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday evening starts with a social gathering at 5:30 pm, followed by a 6 pm service. Saturday has Torah study at 9:15 am before the 10:45 am service, and the choir sings at some Friday services. The site does not say how long services last or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Arrive by 5:30 pm if you want the pre-Shabbat gathering before the 6 pm service.
Use the Green Street entrance at 1339 Green St., as the site directs.
Watch the livestream first if you would like to see a service before going in person.
Office hours are weekdays 8:30 am to 5 pm, if you want to ask questions by phone at 215.627.6747.

records.notes: Tier 1 called Breaking Bread on Broad a Wednesday gathering. The program page describes a Wednesday distribution of food, diapers and hygiene supplies outside the Green Street entrance, so the summary and schedule were corrected; its time is not stated. Service times agree on the homepage and the Our Services page. online_ok is true because services are livestreamed. No page read states membership dues or a visitor policy. The Calendar and Event Registrations pages were not read. No nearest SEPTA stop is recorded because no page names one.

records.name: Consortium Dedicated to Health Equity Education (CDHE)
records.summary: A coalition of Greater Philadelphia medical schools that works to bring more people from diverse backgrounds into medicine. It runs a yearly equity summit, a pre-med pathway for college sophomores, and a mentorship network.
records.what_you_do: Register for the yearly summit, or apply to the PADMed pathway if you are a college sophomore at a Greater Philadelphia university. PADMed asks for a 3.2 GPA or higher and a grade of B minus or better in core science courses. Scholars also get access to the mentorship network.

schedule.text: A yearly one-day summit, 8 am to 4 pm. PADMed scholars attend monthly programming through the academic year.

cost.text: The summit fee is not stated on the site. For PADMed scholars, the site says the program covers summer housing, transportation, and a food stipend, and provides SEPTA passes and meals for in-person sessions.

first_step.how: Register for the summit through the events page, or, if you are a college sophomore, use the Apply Today button on the PADMed page.
first_step.basis: The summit is open to anyone who registers. PADMed needs an application and grade requirements, so it is not an open door.
first_step.what_to_expect: A summit visit is a full day, 8 am to 4 pm, with a keynote, interactive workshops such as restorative practices and cultural humility, and a poster competition. The site does not say what the summit costs. PADMed scholars meet an advisor each semester and attend monthly programming.
first_visit_tips: Read the full agenda before you register so you can pick the workshops you want.
Email programs@philacdhe.org with PADMed questions before you apply.

records.notes: Site conflict: the events page lists a third annual summit on April 22, 2025 at the National Constitution Center, while the homepage lists the fourth annual summit on April 7, 2026 at the College of Physicians of Philadelphia. The record uses the homepage. The homepage says the Apply Today button opens an email to programs@philacdhe.org, but the PADMed page says it opens an application page. The record gives the PADMed page route, so check it before publishing. The homepage register button may not be a working form, so the events page is used for summit registration. Summit price is not stated on any page read.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A member-run rowing club on the Schuylkill River at Boathouse Row. Adults join through member sponsorship and can row at any level, and young people can take part in summer and junior rowing programs.
records.what_you_do: Members row the club's boats on the river at any level, from novice to masters. The club also runs youth summer and junior rowing programs. The riverfront path in front of the boathouses is public and free year round.

schedule.text: Membership runs year round. Summer programs run on the river, and novice sessions usually run 8 to 11 am, Monday to Thursday.

cost.text: Adult membership dues are $550 a year, plus $150 per seat for boat storage. Summer youth programs are $800 each, and the club confirms fees each season at registration.

requirements.gear: Racing uniforms are not included in the development and junior programs.

first_step.how: Send the membership inquiry form on crescentboatclub.org, or apply to a summer youth program through RegattaCentral. Questions go to board@crescentboatclub.org.
first_step.basis: Adult membership needs two member sponsors and annual dues before a first row. The youth Novice program is written for people who have never rowed, but it also needs an application and a fee.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult members can row at any level, but coaching is not part of membership, so people who have never rowed arrange their own coaching, and several members coach privately. Summer youth programs include a Novice program that teaches boat handling and crew rowing, and parents attend an organizational meeting. The page does not describe a first outing for adults.
first_visit_tips: Read the By-laws, Rules and Safety page before your first practice, since the club requires athletes and parents to read it.
Racing uniforms are not included in the development and junior programs, so plan for that cost.
Walk the public riverfront path in front of the boathouses to see the setting before you apply.
Contact board@crescentboatclub.org before you pay if you are not sure which summer program fits.

records.notes: Conflict on the club's own pages: the membership page says the Novice program is for juniors only, while the youth page says it also takes adults. The record says only that Novice is for people who have never rowed. The newest dated news item is from May 2025, and the calendar is an external embed with no dated events, so status stays probably_active. Dues figures come from the membership page as read on 2026-10-08; check them before publishing. The event-space cleaning fee is left out because it applies to event rentals, not membership.

records.name: Crochet Circle at Lutheran Settlement House
records.summary: A weekly crochet circle at the Lutheran Settlement House Fishtown office for adults 55 and older. Volunteer instructors help people make friends, get better at crochet, or learn from the start.
records.what_you_do: Come on a Thursday morning to crochet with others and get help from volunteer instructors. No registration is needed.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the page. Ask the office whether there is a charge or supplies to bring.

first_step.how: Walk into the LSH Fishtown office at 1340 Frankford Ave on a Thursday between 9 and 10 am. No registration is needed.
first_step.basis: The page says anyone 55 and older can come, that people can learn crochet from the start, and that no registration is needed, so the way in is clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each visit is one hour, from 9 to 10 am on a Thursday, at the Fishtown office. Volunteer instructors help people make friends, improve their crochet, or start from scratch. The page does not say whether supplies are provided or whether there is a charge.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at (215) 426-8610 before your first visit to ask about supplies and cost.
Ask about parking and transit on the call, since the page does not describe either.
Arrive a few minutes early so you have time to find your way in.

records.notes: Tier 1 fields carried over. The senior services page names a wider program staff contact with an extension; not added because the circle has its own office phone. Parking, transit and accessibility are not described on either page, so access is left out. The volunteer opportunities page was not read.

records.name: Cross Community Service Center
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) learning, trains teachers, provides educators to K to 12 schools, and helps adults build work skills.
records.what_you_do: Adults can join the career program, which covers computer and information technology skills, resume and cover letter writing, programming practice, and professional leadership. Schools can use the group for educator training and staffing in computer science, math, ESL, and world languages. The group also runs K to 12 STEM programs for children and youth.

first_step.how: Call 267-466-6439 and ask when the Adult Career Program next starts and how to enroll.
first_step.basis: The site lists an adult career program, but its Join page is about working at the organization, and the site gives no enrollment steps, dates, costs or eligibility.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe class times, how long a course runs, what it costs, or what a first session is like. The phone, email and office address are the only ways in that the site publishes, so expect to ask about each part on the first call.
first_visit_tips: Ask about cost, class times, and who the program is for on your first call, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The programs page lists K to 12 STEM programs, an adult career program, and educator training and staffing, with no dates, costs or enrollment steps. The Join page is about working at the organization, not program enrollment. The career category and job clubs interest were added for the adult career program. Confidence stays low because no dated evidence was found.

records.name: Delaware Valley Orienteering Association
records.summary: A club that runs about 45 public orienteering events a year, where people use a map and compass to find checkpoints in parks. Beginners always get instruction at events.
records.what_you_do: Walk or jog a course with a map and compass, punching checkpoints along the way. Beginners get instruction and can take part without experience.

schedule.text: About 45 events a year at parks and environmental centers. Most start between 10 am and 1 pm, with registration until 1 pm and courses closing around 3:30 or 4 pm.

locations.label: Parks and environmental centers in eastern PA, northern DE, northern MD, and central and southern NJ

cost.text: Members pay reduced event fees and get a quarterly newsletter and library checkout. Event and map prices are in a Google Doc linked from the club's info page, so check it before you go. You can join or renew online.

first_step.how: Pick an event on the club's Event Schedule and arrive before 1 pm to register.
first_step.basis: The Learn section is the club's starting point for new people, and the club says beginners always get instruction at events.
first_step.what_to_expect: An event runs about 10 am to 1 pm, and you walk or jog a course with a map and compass. Courses are printed on the map in colors from White to Red, and the White course is the beginner level that several events offer. Some events run a beginners clinic that starts at 10 am.
first_visit_tips: Arrive before 1 pm, because the last start is at 1 pm.
Look for a White course or a beginners clinic in the event listing.
Check the linked price sheet before you go, since prices are not on the main pages.
The events listed from October 2026 to May 2027 are all outside Philadelphia city, so plan on a drive.

records.notes: Verdict question for the orchestrator: none of the 15 events on the schedule for October 18, 2026 to May 1, 2027 is in Philadelphia city or a Philadelphia park. Events are in Chester, Lancaster and other PA counties, NJ, DE, and one national championship in Arizona. The club serves eastern PA broadly, so the verdict is left at publish with in_city false. The owner should decide whether this is out_of_area. The mailing address on the info page is in Spring City (Chester County), not a meeting place. Orienteering has no vocabulary tag, so hiking is used. The six-fetch cap was reached before the Beginner's Home page (learn/begin/index.php) and the beginner FAQ were read, so no equipment or fee facts were taken from them. The FAQ found by search looks older and gives fees that conflict with the price sheet. The tier 1 PDF schedule could not be read (compressed binary), so last_sign_of_life now uses the schedule page, which lists upcoming events from October 2026. The schedule URL redirected to events/sked, which was followed.

records.name: Dereyk Morris Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia foundation whose site says it supports incarcerated people through education. Its office on South Broad Street is open on weekdays, and the site asks for volunteers, but it does not describe its programs. The site also sells paid personal training.
records.what_you_do: Ask about volunteering by phone or on a weekday visit to the office. The site has a 'We need Volunteers' heading and a team application form, but it does not say what volunteers do.

schedule.text: Office hours are 9 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday. The site does not list program times.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee for volunteering. Paid training is sold on the site: one-on-one at $600, bootcamp classes at $180, and a 12-week program at $950. The page does not say whether the first two are per session or per package.

first_step.how: Call 267-325-1686 on a weekday between 9 am and 5 pm and ask what volunteer roles are open and how to start.
first_step.basis: The site asks for volunteers and has a team form, but it does not say what volunteers do, how to start, or whether training or a background check is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a volunteer shift or program session involves, how long it lasts, or who takes part. The team application form asks for a resume, and the page does not say whether it is for volunteers or staff.
first_visit_tips: Ask on the phone what a first volunteer role involves before you visit.
Ask whether a background check or orientation is needed before you commit.
The Upcoming Events page lists no events, so ask whether any programs are running now.

records.notes: Verdict question for the orchestrator: the only offerings the site describes are paid fitness services (personal training, bootcamp classes, a 12-week program) sold through a booking system. No community or reentry program is described, and the only statement of purpose is the homepage tagline. Under the rule for businesses with no community program, this may need to be hidden. It is left at publish with low confidence rather than decided here. Tier 1 said the office welcomes visits. The pages read this time give office hours but do not say visitors are welcome, so drop_in is left out.
